summary: @picsart/ai-sdk ships alternate-runtime install-time dropper executing obfuscated Bun bundle
details: The package advertises itself as a type-safe AI SDK library with main=./index.js and a single runtime dependency (fflate), but its declared preinstall hook (node setup.mjs) downloads the Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ into a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and uses it to execFileSync a bundled sibling file math_init.js on every install. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-CJS bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header, WV8StW string-array shuffle, numeric/char table n7gIxM, custom charset decoder hc1jfK9) with no readable identifiers or URLs, and is not referenced anywhere from index.js — it exists only to be run by the downloaded Bun runtime at preinstall. setup.mjs itself is javascript-obfuscator-style renamed (_0x* identifiers, string-key indirection objects). The alternate-runtime choice hides the executed payload from Node-based static analysis, and the file name math_init has no relationship to any advertised AI-SDK feature. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: install-time execution of opaque bytes under a runtime fetched at install, on a package whose stated purpose does not require Bun.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
